title: US SPR & Storage Watch
dek: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and commercial crude stocks, SPR inventory, the 2026 exchange/refill mechanics, and Cushing.

claims.text: DOE's per-site grade table as of August 20, 2026 showed 101.8 million barrels of sweet and 192.3 million of sour (294.1 million total), or roughly 34.6% sweet and 65.4% sour. DOE defines sweet as sulfur content no greater than 0.5% by weight and sour as greater than 0.5% but less than 2.0%; DOE's stated design ratio is about 40% sweet to 60% sour, based on likely US refinery needs, especially on the Gulf Coast.
claims.source: US Department of Energy (SPR Quick Facts)

claims.text: DOE reported the reserve at 284.9 million barrels as of September 11, split 96.8 million sweet and 188.1 million sour (Reuters). Against the August 20 DOE table, sweet drew about 5.0 million barrels and sour about 4.2 million over roughly three weeks, with sweet leaving slightly faster in absolute terms; the sweet share slipped to about 34.0%, drifting further from DOE's 40% design target. Note the September 11 split comes from secondary reporting of a DOE figure, not the published Quick Facts grade table.
claims.source: Reuters (via Permian Basin Oil and Gas Magazine)

claims.text: The September 11 total sat about 32.5 million barrels above the 252.4-million-barrel minimum Congress mandates, so the exchange program has limited drawdown room left before hitting the statutory floor. DOE says it has secured cancellation of 140 million barrels of congressionally mandated sales scheduled for fiscal years 2024 through 2027, so there is no forced-sale overhang on the forward calendar.
claims.source: Reuters (via Permian Basin Oil and Gas Magazine); US Department of Energy (energy.gov)

claims.text: Refill buying stays token: the Senate-passed July 2025 budget bill cut SPR crude purchase funding to $171 million from the House's $1.3 billion, roughly 3 million barrels at prevailing prices, and kept the repeal of the last 7 million barrels of congressionally mandated sales through fiscal year 2027 (final legislative status unconfirmed).

Near term the program still leans bearish for sour: Secretary Wright said in mid-September that another round of exchange loans is 'a very real possibility', with about 38.5 million barrels of the 172-million-barrel authorized program still unallocated. The reversal is scheduled: borrowed crude is expected to start returning early in 2027 and run through 2029 at roughly 1.25 barrels returned per barrel borrowed, implying about 35 to 40 million premium barrels on top of the principal that the market must supply back to the reserve.
claims.source: Turkiye New Updates (citing Argus Media via Anadolu Agency); BOE Report (citing Reuters)

claims.text: The American Petroleum Institute's weekly estimate for the week ending Sep 25 showed US commercial crude stocks rising 1.019 million barrels, a second straight weekly build against an analyst consensus cited by OilPrice expecting a 1.9 million barrel draw, with gasoline up 2.991 million barrels and distillates down 286,000 barrels; the official EIA weekly report was due later on Sep 30.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 25, 2026; reported Sep 29, 2026

claims.text: Commercial crude stocks rose 3.0 million barrels to 426.4 million barrels in the week ending September 18, roughly 2 percent above the five-year average, while analysts surveyed by Reuters had expected a 641,000-barrel draw. Crude at the Cushing, Oklahoma delivery hub rose 2.2 million barrels to 23.7 million barrels.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 18, 2026; published Sep 23, 2026; accessed 2026-09-28

claims.text: The Energy Information Administration's (EIA) report for the week ending September 18, 2026 (released September 23) showed commercial crude stocks rising 3.0 million barrels to 426.4 million, about 2 percent above the five-year seasonal average, as refinery runs fell 2.8 percentage points to 94.0 percent and crude inputs dropped 519,000 b/d to 16.8 million b/d. Gasoline stocks fell 1.7 million barrels to 206 million (6 percent below the five-year average) and distillate stocks fell 428,000 barrels to 107.4 million (12 percent below); US crude production was 13.9 million b/d with imports of 5.9 million b/d and exports of 3.3 million b/d.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 18, 2026; published Sep 23, 2026; accessed 2026-09-24

claims.text: Cushing, Oklahoma (the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) delivery hub for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures) built 2.3 million barrels in the September 18 week to 23.7 million barrels, an 11 percent jump after falling to 21.5 million the prior week. That is roughly 31 percent of the hub's reported 75-to-76-million-barrel working capacity and still close to the roughly 20-million-barrel level traders treat as the operational minimum for pump suction and pipeline pressure ('tank bottoms'); the hub touched a summer low near 18.6 million barrels in late June.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 18, 2026; published Sep 23, 2026; accessed 2026-09-24
claims.source: Morningstar (citing EIA); Oklahoma Energy Today (citing EIA)

claims.text: After Politico reported the White House was preparing a 90-day diesel export ban, the White House denied the report on Sep 23 while President Trump said he backed a ban; Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the same day that a ban would not work and could push up gasoline and jet fuel prices, pushing instead for voluntary refiner cooperation. US diesel futures fell 4 percent on the news, with the national average diesel price near 6.52 dollars a gallon per AAA.

Senators Susan Collins and Angus King of Maine wrote to President Trump on Sep 22 asking him to release home heating oil from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, noting Maine households are paying about 675 dollars more per tank fill than last year and diesel has surged past 6.50 dollars a gallon. The 1-million-barrel reserve, stored at four sites from Maine to New Jersey, holds roughly 10 days of regional supply and has not been tapped since Hurricane Sandy in 2012.
claims.vintage: Letter sent Sep 22, 2026; published Sep 23, 2026; accessed 2026-09-28

claims.text: Atlantic coast distillate inventories fell to 19.3 million barrels in the final week of August, the lowest weekly level since records began in 1990, recovering only to 21.6 million by September 11, while US distillate exports hit a record 1.88 million barrels per day in late July. Canada's 320,000-barrel-per-day Saint John refinery, a major supplier of ultra low sulfur diesel to the northeastern US, is undergoing a 75-day maintenance program from early September to mid-November.

Distillate stocks (diesel and heating oil) were 107.4 million barrels in the week ending September 18, about 12 percent below the five-year seasonal average, and the US entered autumn with refiners near their ceiling: distillate production averaged 5.1 million b/d from January through August (the most since 2019) and utilization hit 97 to 98 percent in early September. Diesel averaged $6.52 per gallon (American Automobile Association) and heating oil traded near a record around $5 per gallon, roughly 120 percent above a year earlier, while net distillate exports sat near or above their 2021-2025 high since February and Russia planned to extend diesel export restrictions through October.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 18, 2026; reported Sep 18-23, 2026; accessed 2026-09-24
claims.source: Daily Caller News Foundation (citing EIA and AAA); TradingEconomics (citing EIA); The Autowire (citing EIA)

claims.text: The Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve holds about one million barrels of heating oil, roughly five days of regional supply, and a release requires the heating-oil-over-crude price spread to run more than 60 percent above its five-year average for seven straight days while continuing to widen. Unlike the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), the Northeast reserve holds refined fuel that can go directly to heating-oil markets, but a price spike alone does not automatically trigger a release; it must meet the statutory dislocation standard (National Energy Assistance Directors Association).
claims.source: Daily Caller News Foundation (quoting National Energy Assistance Directors Association)

claims.text: The Energy Information Administration's (EIA) September Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) raised its 2026 distillate crack spread forecast to $1.57 per gallon, up 20.8 percent from the August estimate, and lifted the 2027 figure to $1.25, formalizing the market's bet that refinery margins stay elevated while global middle-distillate balances stay tight. Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, Russia's diesel export curbs, and Middle East supply risk are cited as the drivers.
claims.vintage: EIA September 2026 STEO; reported Sep 21, 2026; accessed 2026-09-24
claims.source: The Autowire (citing EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook)

claims.text: The Department of Energy issued a request for proposal on Sep 29 for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels of SPR crude from the Big Hill and Bryan Mound sites, with deliveries under awarded exchanges scheduled for November and December 2026 and bids due by 11:00 a.m. Central Time on Oct 6; DOE says five prior solicitations awarded more than 133 million barrels and earlier exchanges returned an average 25 percent premium.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright clarified in a CNBC interview that Venezuela's heavy crude would not be placed directly into reserve salt caverns but could be swapped for light or medium US barrels, because much of Venezuela's oil is heavier and higher in sulfur than the crude traditionally held in the reserve. Analysts quoted in the piece cautioned that many of the Venezuelan fields would need years of development and reinvestment before producing meaningful volumes.

In June 2026 the Department of Energy (DOE) awarded contracts for a further approximately 53.3 million barrels of Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) exchange crude across all four sites (Bayou Choctaw, Bryan Mound, Big Hill, West Hackberry) under its late-April request for proposal, carrying an approximately 28 percent return premium (15.1 million barrels). DOE said about 35 million barrels had been delivered to market to that point and that earlier phases had awarded roughly 80 million barrels (45.2 plus 8.5 plus 26 million).

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in mid-September that the US has lent more than 130 million barrels (over three-quarters of the 172-million-barrel authorized exchange), with about 38.5 million barrels still unallocated and another round of loans 'a very real possibility' while front-month West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades roughly 25 percent above the six-month contract. Borrowed crude is expected to start returning early in 2027 and continue through 2029 at roughly 1.25 barrels returned per barrel borrowed, implying about 35 to 40 million premium barrels on top of the principal.
claims.source: Turkiye New Updates (citing Argus Media via Anadolu Agency); BOE Report (citing Reuters)

claims.text: Other International Energy Agency (IEA) members' announced contributions to the 400-million-barrel coordinated release included 22.46 million barrels from South Korea and 13.5 million barrels from the United Kingdom, with Germany, Austria, and Japan also releasing stock (Japan's releases began in mid-March), per reporting in late July 2026. Aggregate member delivery progress beyond these pledges has not been published in a single authoritative ledger.

OilPrice's weekly snapshot put the SPR at 283.8 million barrels after another 800,000 barrels left the reserve in the week ending Sep 25, against the reserve's roughly 714 million barrel design capacity.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 25, 2026; reported Sep 29, 2026

claims.text: The reserve held 284.6 million barrels in the week ending September 18, down 29.9 percent from a year earlier and down 130.5 million barrels since reaching 415.1 million on March 27, leaving it at roughly 40 percent of its 714-million-barrel design capacity across four Gulf Coast sites.
claims.vintage: Data: week ending Sep 18, 2026; published ~Sep 25, 2026; accessed 2026-09-28

claims.text: The Energy Information Administration (EIA) weekly series puts the Strategic Petroleum Reserve at its lowest weekly level since November 1982; Brookings Institution analyst Samantha Gross warned that aggressive pumping can damage the salt caverns themselves.

The Department of Energy's (DOE) Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) Quick Facts page put per-site inventory at 294.1 million barrels as of August 20, 2026: Bryan Mound 142.5 million (48 percent of the reserve), Big Hill 89.1 million, West Hackberry 30.5 million, and Bayou Choctaw 32.0 million. The quality split was 101.8 million barrels sweet and 192.3 million sour, meaning roughly 65 percent of the remaining reserve is sour crude.
claims.source: US Department of Energy (SPR Quick Facts)

claims.text: The Department of Energy (DOE) lists the Strategic Petroleum Reserve's (SPR) maximum nominal drawdown capability at 4.4 million b/d with oil able to enter the market 13 days after a presidential decision, but effective capacity is lower: Big Hill's drawdown capability is currently zero because of a construction outage and West Hackberry is limited to 0.75 million b/d by low inventory.
claims.source: US Department of Energy (SPR Quick Facts); Wikipedia (citing DOE facility data)

claims.text: From about 415 million barrels when the exchanges began in mid-March to 284.6 million in the week ending September 18, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) drew roughly 130 million barrels in about 27 weeks, an average pace of roughly 0.7 million b/d (Heavy Reading calculation from Department of Energy (DOE) and Energy Information Administration (EIA) figures).
claims.source: Heavy Reading calculation (DOE via TS2.Tech; EIA via Energy Factbook)

claims.text: The Senate-passed July 2025 budget bill cut Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) crude purchase funding to $171 million from the House's $1.3 billion, enough for roughly 3 million barrels instead of about 20 million at prevailing prices, according to Rapidan Energy cited in the reporting; the same bill kept the repeal of the last 7 million barrels of congressionally mandated SPR sales through fiscal year 2027 (Reuters).
